# sopuli report

Read-only reports across the declared targets (UC-5).

A report reads every account on each declared target, declared or not, and
changes nothing. These are the only commands that list the accounts the
config does not declare (invariant 5).

## sopuli report accounts

```
sopuli report accounts [OPTIONS]
```

Check every account on each target against the `reports:` rules.

One table per target, problems first. A check ends as a problem, OK, not
checked (the target cannot read the value truthfully, such as a common
account's lock on a PDB), no rule (the config states nothing to compare), or
not applicable (the product has no such thing, such as a profile on
PostgreSQL). An account counts as OK only when every check had a rule and
passed.

Exit 0 when nothing is wrong, 1 when a target could not be reached, 3 when a
check found a problem or a profile a rule or policy expects is missing on a
target, and 4 when something could not be checked. An account
the config does not declare is listed as information and never changes the
exit code. It runs on Oracle, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB. On MariaDB the
lock and the lifetime come from the optional view `sopuli.account_state`,
and are not checked where the view is absent or cannot be used.

Options:

- `--select` `K=V[,K=V]` (repeatable): Keep only targets carrying every label given. Repeat for more labels.
- `--target` `NAME` (repeatable): Keep only this target. Repeat to add more.
- `--group` `NAME` (repeatable): Keep only targets in this group. Repeat to add more.
- `--all`: List every account, including the ones that passed every check.

It also takes the [global options](README.md#global-options).

## sopuli report history

```
sopuli report history [OPTIONS]
```

Show when each managed password was rotated or reset, from the store.

For each application account, every change of its own `rotated_at` stamp
the store still keeps; for each personal account, every version of its
reset record. Each history says where it starts and how many earlier
versions are gone. The database's own date of the last password change is
shown beside it and never compared. No password is read into the report.

Exit 0 when every history was read, 1 when a target or a store gave no
answer, and 4 when a history has a gap or the store keeps no versions.
Oracle, PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB can run it. The database's date comes
from Oracle and MySQL, and on MariaDB from the optional view
`sopuli.account_state`. PostgreSQL keeps none. Where there is no date, the
report says why it is unknown.

Options:

- `--select` `K=V[,K=V]` (repeatable): Keep only targets carrying every label given. Repeat for more labels.
- `--target` `NAME` (repeatable): Keep only this target. Repeat to add more.
- `--group` `NAME` (repeatable): Keep only targets in this group. Repeat to add more.
- `--account` `NAME`: Show only this account.

It also takes the [global options](README.md#global-options).

## sopuli report privileges

```
sopuli report privileges [OPTIONS]
```

Show each account's effective privileges, through every role.

For each account `report accounts` covers: its roles, its system privileges
with where each comes from, and its object and column privileges as counts
by privilege and object type. `--detail` lists every privilege with each
role path. A privilege held through a role that is not a default role counts
too, and is marked. The report judges nothing.

Exit 0 when every part was read, 1 when a target could not be reached, and 4
when a part could not be read, such as without the optional grant on
Oracle's privilege views, or another database of a PostgreSQL cluster,
which a target cannot see into and no other declared target connects to
at the same host and port, or MariaDB's global level. Oracle,
PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB can run this report.

Options:

- `--select` `K=V[,K=V]` (repeatable): Keep only targets carrying every label given. Repeat for more labels.
- `--target` `NAME` (repeatable): Keep only this target. Repeat to add more.
- `--group` `NAME` (repeatable): Keep only targets in this group. Repeat to add more.
- `--account` `NAME`: Show only this account. It may be one the config does not declare.
- `--detail`: List every privilege, with each role path.
- `--public`: Also list the grants to PUBLIC, once per target.

It also takes the [global options](README.md#global-options).
